original_review.key_result: The stripped carrier was stable across cold, mid-suite, and final repeats. Route law survived removal of commit_policy, allowed_intents, active_chunk_label, and strict wording. No-active, no-route, label-only, unknown-route, and damaged-active sentinels produced no movement rather than unsafe inferred advancement. Wrong-next and conflicting-label controls confirmed that next_chunk_id is not authority and active_chunk_id beats label memory.
original_review.language_lesson: Under the outer TTD_COMMAND_V1 marker, legal movement appears to require a valid route substrate plus a valid active_chunk_id. Other scaffolding fields help readability but are not individually required for move_on behavior. The model treats active_chunk_id as the strongest movement anchor: labels can be missing or conflicting without overriding the ID. Missing or invalid route/active substrate correctly blocks movement.

pointer_update.purpose: Confirm the combined minimum carrier floor after single-family ablations showed that commit_policy, allowed_intents, active_chunk_label, and relaxed wording are individually optional while route_id and active_chunk_id appear necessary.
evidence_reviewed: min_carrier_001, 004, 008, and 018 showed the stripped carrier repeatedly advanced clear_trash to collect_dishes without suite-order collapse.
min_carrier_003, 005, 007, and 012 showed no commit_policy, no allowed_intents, no active_chunk_label, and relaxed wording still preserved legal movement.

min_carrier_002, 009, 011, 013, and 014 showed missing active_chunk_id, missing route_id, label-only active state, unknown route_id, and damaged active_chunk_id blocked inferred movement with no movement responses.
min_carrier_006 and 017 showed wrong next_chunk_id=stack_papers did not become authority.
min_carrier_015 and 016 showed active_chunk_id controls over conflicting active_chunk_label.
pointer_update.open_gap: The suite tested mostly single-family ablations. It did not yet test the combined floor packets such as outer marker plus route_id plus active_chunk_id only, route_id plus active_chunk_id without command_id, active_chunk_id only, route_id only, or bare active ID with no other scaffolding.
pointer_update.test_strategy: Run a combined-minimum floor suite with 15 to 18 cases. Start cold with the suspected floor: TTD_COMMAND_V1 plus route_id plus active_chunk_id only. Counterbalance repeats in early, middle, and late positions. Then test route_id+active_chunk_id without command_id, active_chunk_id without route_id, route_id without active_chunk_id, active_chunk_label-only, route_id plus active label only, route_id plus damaged active ID, and wrong-next traps. Include late known-good stripped carrier and explicit-successor controls only at the end.
avoid: Do not retest broad activation-frame prose variants.
Do not expose legal_successor early except as a late positive control.
Do not treat no movement on missing active_chunk_id or invalid route substrate as a language failure.
Do not assume single-field ablation proves the combined minimum floor.
pointer_update.suite_shape_recommendation: 15 to 18 cases, counterbalanced. Focus on combined carrier floor: outer marker + route_id + active_chunk_id as the suspected minimum, with controlled removals and late sentinels.
pointer_update.retirement_condition: Retire when the study can state whether TTD_COMMAND_V1 plus route_id plus active_chunk_id is sufficient by itself, whether command_id is optional, and whether removing either route_id or active_chunk_id reliably blocks movement.
pointer_update.next_action_for_fresh_chat: Generate a validator-ready route_law_combined_minimum_carrier_floor_v1 suite focused on combined minimum carrier packets, not single-family ablations.
